title: A US-India trade deal is 'weeks away'
credits: Photos: Chris LeBoutillier, Anders Marlowe / Unsplash · Map: Natural Earth
lines: The United States and India say a big trade deal is almost done.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio began a two-day visit to India on the twentieth of October, landing in Mumbai.
He held talks with India's foreign minister, S. Jaishankar, and visited Jamnagar, home of the world's largest refining complex, run by Reliance Industries.
Rubio told India's News18 channel that he expects a deal within weeks, not months.
Days before the trip, President Trump delayed tariffs on Indian imports.
He also waived tariffs that could have punished India for buying Russian oil.
A law signed in September allows tariffs of up to one hundred percent on the top five buyers of Russian oil. India ranks second, after China.
India imports more than eighty-five percent of the crude oil it needs.
Rubio says India has diversified its energy, but still gets a substantial amount from Russia.
Geography is real, he said. For some countries, it is very difficult to buy energy elsewhere.
Closer US-India trade ties are something Islamabad will be watching closely.
